summary: Full backend + frontend E2E test of SocietyHub. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (33 pytest cases) covering auth/JWT/cookies/lockout, demo-seed idempotency, property/flat/meter/tank CRUD, defaults persistence, tanker auto-calc, readings bulk save, charges + apply-defaults idempotency, payments/payouts, statement engine math (verified against manual calculation), meter_rollback + negative_reserve flags, month reset with lock/carry-in/opening-reading carry-over, 423 on locked writes, MIS CSV+PDF, uploads (image/video/reject + download), role restrictions. 29/33 passed. Frontend: Playwright flows for login (valid/invalid), dashboard per-flat table (numbers reconciled manually against seeded data: 24000 L / Rs.3650 / avg 0.1521 / reserve 2400 L / recurring 6800 / maint 8600 all correct), water tanker live auto-sum + per-litre + save/delete + media upload with thumbnail, readings save + rollback flag, Setup CRUD (building/flat/meter/tank + deletes) and defaults persistence after reload, charges apply-defaults idempotency + manual recurring with person/payer override + one-time maintenance bifurcation, reconciliation (tenant payment reduces net and lands in Tenant paid column, payout increases net, fronted contributions deducted, red owes / green owed), month reset dialog + lock + read-only + carry-in Rs.10,011 into September + closing 1120 becoming next-month opening, MIS on-screen + valid CSV (520 B) and PDF (2.8 KB) downloads, resident role restriction, mobile 390x844. All destructive tests were run on a throwaway 'QA Tower UI' building; the demo building was restored to its original figures and left open.

critical.issue: Auth bypass: the endpoint only checks that the `auth` query param is non-empty and never validates the JWT, so any unauthenticated caller can download any uploaded photo/video by id (verified: `?auth=any-garbage` returned 200 + file bytes).

Owner/resident data leak: /api/statement is scoped to the user's flat, but MIS export is not — resident tenant1@societyhub.com downloaded the full-building CSV containing flats 102/201/202 owner names and balances. The list endpoints and /api/properties are also readable by residents for any property_id.

Brute-force lockout ineffective in this deployment: the lockout identifier is `client.host:email`, and behind the ingress the observed client IP alternates between replica IPs (10.208.135.204/.205), so 7 consecutive bad passwords produced 7x401 and the counters split 4/3 — 429 never fires. Key the counter on email (and/or X-Forwarded-For) instead.

minor.issue: CORS_ORIGINS=* with allow_credentials=True returns `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` together with `Allow-Credentials: true` (and the preflight OPTIONS response has no allow-credentials header at all). Invalid combination for cookie auth — harmless today only because the SPA is same-origin. Use explicit origins.
storage.put_object/get_object use blocking `requests` inside async handlers, blocking the event loop for the whole upload/download (40 MB limit). Wrap in run_in_threadpool or use httpx.AsyncClient.

Duplicate suppression is per charge_type, so if an admin has already entered a manual charge of that type the fixed monthly default is silently skipped (no feedback distinguishing 'already applied' from 'skipped because manual entry exists').

ui_bugs.issue: After confirming 'Close & reset month' the toast says 'August 2026 locked. September 2026 is now open.' but the app stays on the locked August period (switcher shows 'August 2026 · locked' and all forms become read-only). The user must manually switch periods; the spec expects the new month to open.
When the locked banner is shown the sidebar keeps `top-14`, so the banner overlays the first nav item — 'Dashboard' is half hidden/unclickable region behind the amber banner.

For a rolled-back meter the readings table displays consumption -500 (amber) while the engine bills 0 L for that meter; the two views disagree. Show 0 (or 'flagged / excluded') to match the statement.
React console error on every login: 'Cannot update a component (BrowserRouter) while rendering a different component (Login)' — setState/navigate called during render.
Toasts render top-right and completely cover the property switcher and period switcher for ~4s after every save.

integration_issues.issue: Resident sees the property switcher listing ALL buildings and is left on whichever property is selected globally; on a building where they have no flat MyDues shows 'No statement for this period' instead of defaulting to their own building/flat. Nav restriction and /setup redirect work correctly.

issues: Horizontal overflow of the page shell: dashboard +115px, Water tanker-form tab +401px, Water readings tab +115px (measured scrollWidth-clientWidth); screenshots show content clipped on the left. Header (hamburger + logo + 150px property select + 130px period select + logout) alone cannot fit in 390px.
Sidebar hamburger toggle, 48px-tall number inputs and live total/per-litre calc all work correctly on mobile.

action_items: Validate the JWT in GET /api/files/{id} (currently any non-empty ?auth value grants access).
Scope /api/mis/export (and list endpoints /api/flats, /api/charges, /api/payments, /api/tankers, /api/properties) for owner/resident roles.
Key login-attempt lockout on the email (or X-Forwarded-For) — client.host varies per ingress replica so 429 never triggers.
Set explicit CORS origins instead of '*' when allow_credentials=True.
After a successful month reset, switch the UI to the newly opened next month.
Fix locked-banner overlap of the first sidebar nav item and the mobile horizontal overflow (header controls + water form grid).
Make the readings table show 0 consumption for a flagged rolled-back meter so it matches the statement.
Fix setState-during-render in Login.jsx; move the toaster so it does not cover the property/period switchers.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:709 download_file — presence check `if not A.extract_token(request) and not auth` is not authentication; decode the token (or a signed short-lived file token) before serving bytes.

server.py:597 mis_export uses Depends(current_user) with no role scoping while /statement filters rows — same data must be filtered in both places (and the totals block in /statement still exposes building-wide figures to residents).
auth.py:103 lockout window keyed on request.client.host defeats itself behind a multi-replica proxy; also nothing rate-limits /auth/register.
storage.py uses sync requests inside async FastAPI handlers — offload to a threadpool.
server.py is 836 lines and mixes auth, CRUD, exports and seeding; consider splitting into routers (auth/setup/water/charges/reports).

success_rate.frontend: ~82% (all core admin flows pass; 5 UI/mobile defects)

seed_data_creation: Used the existing demo seed (Sunrise Residency). Created and then deleted a throwaway 'QA Tower UI' building via the UI (flat A1, meter, tank, charges, payments, tanker with uploaded PNG, month reset). Pytest creates and deletes TEST_* properties. Demo data was restored to its original figures (24000 L / Rs.3650 / 21600 L consumed / Rs.6800 recurring / Rs.8600 maintenance, period 2026-08 still open, no flags).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Regression suite: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/backend_test.py -v` (uses pytest.ini -n 2 --dist loadscope; each class gets its own TEST_ property so it is safe to re-run and self-cleans). The 4 known failures are the real defects listed above (files auth bypass, resident MIS leak, lockout, CORS). Demo month is 2026-08 and is intentionally left OPEN — do not reset it; do destructive month-reset tests on a throwaway building as done here. Frontend selectors used: nav-*, setup-tab-*, water-tab-*, tanker-*, reading-opening/closing-{meter label}, apply-defaults-btn, recurring-*/adhoc-*, payment-*, month-reset-btn/reset-confirm-btn, export-csv-btn/export-pdf-btn, tanker-media-file-input (set_input_files works). Note charge-type option labels are 'Cleaning / Maid', 'Sweeper', 'Building Security', 'Common Electricity', 'Miscellaneous' (not the raw keys).
rca_of_the_issue: files auth bypass: download_file only tests truthiness of the `auth` query param, never decoding it. MIS leak: mis_export shares build_statement with /statement but skips the owner/resident row-filter block. Lockout: identifier = f'{request.client.host}:{email}' and the preview ingress terminates connections from multiple pod IPs, so each replica keeps its own sub-threshold counter. UI reset: Reconcile calls /periods/reset and refreshes data but never calls setMonth(next_month), so AppContext keeps the now-locked month selected.
